title: Costs rebuild 2 · piece 1: Harbour request-usage intake, store and per-record pricing (nothing reads it yet)
description:
**Piece 1 of LIN-4195** (Harbour). It covers D1–D5 plus indexes, erasure and docs. It deploys on its own, and no figure moves.

**Store (D1, D2):**

* Create a new collection, `request-usage`. Do **not** use `llm-call-log`, which about 42 readers treat as Harbour's own calls.
* Add a `RequestUsageStore` with these fields:
  * `requestId`;
  * `rootItemId`: set by Harbour from the taken row via `anchorOf`. Never trust it from the body;
  * `itemId` and `issueIdentifier`: stored, and nothing reads them in this ticket;
  * `harness`, `model`, `effort`, `lane`, and `agent` (`main` or the subagent id);
  * the five token fields;
  * optional native `costUsd`;
  * `at` and `updatedAt`.
* Unique key: `{urlKey, rootItemId, requestId}`. No stored price.
* Add `listForAnchors(urlKey, anchors)` with a projection of only the needed fields. Piece 4 is its only caller.

**Intake (D3):**

* Add `POST /api/dispatch/usage/:itemId` and its runner-token twin `POST /api/proxy/runner/usage/:id`, with one shared handler. Follow the precedent of `validateFeedbackBody` shared by the two feedback routes.
* Use the same token auth and the same ownership rule as feedback (`status:'taken'`, taken by this token).
* Body: `{records:[...]}`, at most 100 per call.
* Upsert: `$max` on the five token fields and `costUsd`, `$setOnInsert` on the identity fields. Use `bulkWrite`, with an E11000 retry for concurrent upserts, as `lib/kpi-daily-rollup.js` does.
* Response: `{applied:[requestIds], rejected:[{requestId, reason}]}`.

**Guards (D4):**

* An all-zero-token record is accepted, not stored, and reported as applied.
* A record whose prompt tokens (input + cache read + cache write) exceed 2,000,000 is rejected.
* Non-finite or negative fields, over-long ids, and a missing `requestId` are rejected per record, with a reason.

**Pricing (D5):**

* Add per-request pricing in `lib/model-pricing.js` (a `perRequest` option or a sibling `priceRequest`; your choice). It uses `selectRateForPrompt` on the record's own prompt size, whatever `harness` says.
* The legacy snapshot path keeps the `crossesThreshold && isRunningTotal` null guard (`lib/model-pricing.js:368`) unchanged.
* **Review note 4:** native `costUsd`, when present, wins over the read-time price for a record. This matches `lib/session-telemetry.js:464`. State it in the code and the docs.

**Registers:**

* `lib/db-indexes.js`: declare the `{urlKey, rootItemId}` index and the unique key (lockstep rule).
* `lib/account-erasure.js` (\~:159): list the new collection.
* Update `lib/proxy-instructions.js` (the endpoint catalogue), `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md`, `docs/architecture/source-map.md` and `scripts/code-shape/areas.json`.

**Witnesses:**

* Against real mongod (precedent: `cost-read-usage-parity.test.js`):
  * posting a request twice leaves one document;
  * a larger repost grows it;
  * a smaller repost leaves it unchanged;
  * two concurrent batches with the same ids leave one document each.
* Pricing:
  * the same tokens and model with `harness:'claude-code'` vs `'opencode'` price identically as a record;
  * a Haiku request over 100k prices at the tier rate;
  * the same tokens as a legacy cumulative snapshot still price null.
* Intake:
  * a zero-token record stores nothing;
  * a record over 2M is rejected;
  * a non-owner token is refused.
* Mutation checks:
  * pricing a record by harness makes the Haiku test fail;
  * insert-if-absent makes the growth test fail.

**Acceptance:**

* The witnesses above pass.
* Replay goldens are unchanged.
* Nothing outside the new route and store reads the collection.

---

**Parent:** LIN-4195 "Costs rebuild 2: one record per model request, summed". Its full design (decisions D1–D14, the replay change list, the witnesses, the order of landing) is in LIN-4195's description under "## Implementation Plan". The plan-review notes are in LIN-4195's comment `eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1`. The numbered notes cited here ("review note N") refer to that comment.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4195's approving plan-review (comment eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1, rev 1)
Grounding commits: Harbour (JKershaw/LinearViewer) `72305215`, runner (JKershaw/simple-dispatcher) `cc2650a`. At breakdown (2026-11-04 \~01:45Z) neither repo had a commit after these.

The parent's approved plan is this piece's starting point; read it in full in LIN-4195's description. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4195.

---

**Implemented (close-out):** merged as [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2265](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2265>) (squash `9cc5ff9c`), deployed. The approved plan (LIN-4195 "## Implementation Plan", D1–D5) was implemented as approved, with the deviations recorded in the review and close-out comments (usage route refuses the single-use Harbour OS feedback token; `updatedAt` advances on repost; limiter reuse). This description held no embedded plan/research sections to prune (the plan lives on LIN-4195), so the problem, scope, witnesses and acceptance above are kept as-is. Full history: task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
**LIN-4198 (piece 1 of LIN-4195): PR is open, CI is green.** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2265

Head `7834e2346646481ddb1029405dc072d5c79d979e`. Checks on that head, run 41768766315: Unit tests pass, E2E shards 1/4 to 4/4 pass, Secret scan (source) pass, CI success pass. Full unit suite 22932 pass, 0 fail.

**Deliberate deviations, for review to judge**
1. The dispatch usage route `POST /api/dispatch/usage/:itemId` refuses the single-use Harbour OS feedback token (401, and the refusal does not spend it). The ticket said "same token auth as feedback". Feedback spends that token on its first successful call, and a runner posts usage in batches, so the second batch would fail.
2. `updatedAt` advances on every repost (`$max` of the post time). The figures do not change; the document does.
3. The `{urlKey, rootItemId}` index is prefix-redundant with the unique key and is kept, as the ticket and lockstep rule ask. On real mongod the planner picks it for `listForAnchors`; without it the unique key answers as a covered scan.
4. The usage routes reuse `feedbackLimiter` and `proxyLimiter`, not tuned limits.

Not covered: the cost read (piece 4), the runner posting records (piece 2), the live measurement (piece 3). The replay check (`scripts/cost-replay.mjs`) exits 1 identically on HEAD and this branch, which is pre-existing LIN-4177 baseline drift. Fixtures and goldens are unchanged.

Left In Progress for review.

**Autopilot (stepper) run summary - LIN-4198, implementation arc**

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2265 (head 7834e2346646481ddb1029405dc072d5c79d979e). CI run 41768766315: Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan (source) and CI success all green on that head. Full unit suite 22,932 pass / 0 fail. Not merged: review then close-out are next.

Beats (one warm session, each judged against the worker's diff in its clone, not just its recap):
1. Store + listForAnchors (minimal projection) + both index specs + erasure row; 28 store tests, 3 mutation witnesses.
2. Per-request pricing (priceRequest, record's own prompt size regardless of harness, finite native costUsd wins); snapshot crossesThreshold && isRunningTotal guard unchanged, characterization tests green before the edit; 2 mutation witnesses.
3. Shared intake handler + both routes (dispatch + runner twin), guards (100 cap, 2M bound, zero-token accepted-not-stored, per-record rejection), rootItemId from anchorOf; 4 mutation witnesses; census/sweep rows added.
4. Registers/docs/source map/areas.json; HTTP test pinning the Harbour OS token refusal (mutation-observed); replay goldens and fixtures untouched.
5. Commit, PR, CI, Linear comment.

Checked by me: existing-test edits are only count/row additions (no assertion weakened); no golden/fixture/replay file in the diff.

For review to judge: (1) usage route refuses the single-use Harbour OS feedback token (ticket said 'same token auth as feedback'; that token is spent on first success, batches would fail) - an engineering call, documented in code, catalogue and docs, pinned by test; (2) updatedAt advances on every repost; (3) {urlKey, rootItemId} index is prefix-redundant but kept per ticket; (4) limiter reuse. Open: scripts/cost-replay.mjs exits 1 identically on HEAD and branch (pre-existing LIN-4177 drift). Commit trailer names Sonnet 5.5 while the workers ran Haiku 5.5 - amendable.

What's left: review, then close-out (merge + Done).

## Review — LIN-4198

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2265, head `7834e2346646481ddb1029405dc072d5c79d979e` (one commit on `1b6c6758`; mergeable).

CI: green on head `7834e234`, run 41768766315 (Unit tests, E2E 1/4–4/4, Secret scan, CI success all SUCCESS). The unit job sets `MONGODB_TEST_URI`, and the real-mongod witness fails hard without it.

### Scope against the plan
The diff matches D1–D5 plus the registers. It adds a new `request-usage` collection (not `llm-call-log`), `RequestUsageStore` with `upsertRecords` and `listForAnchors` (minimal projection), and one shared intake (`lib/request-usage-intake.js`) behind both `POST /api/dispatch/usage/:itemId` and `POST /api/proxy/runner/usage/:id`. It also adds `readTakenForUsage`, which uses the same `ownershipFilterOf` as `addFeedback` (extracted, so the two cannot drift), and sets `rootItemId` from `anchorOf(row)`. Pricing is a sibling function, `priceRequest`, and the snapshot guard is now `!perRequest && crossesThreshold && isRunningTotal`, so the snapshot path behaves exactly as before. Index specs, the erasure row, the proxy catalogue, both architecture docs and `areas.json` are all updated. The diff touches no fixture, golden or replay file. Nothing outside the route and store reads the collection: grep finds it only in db-indexes, account-erasure, the two routes, `routes/proxy.js` wiring and `server.js`.

### Re-ground / regression
- The only commit on `main` since the ticket was created is `1b6c6758` (LIN-4197, piece 0), which is this branch's base.
- Recent history on `model-pricing.js`, `dispatch-store.js` and the routes (`caf33052` LIN-4134 running-total rule, `10b2c82f` LIN-4177, `72305215` LIN-4179):
  - `isRunningTotal` and the snapshot guard are intact.
  - The `takenByTokenId: null` legacy-match comment on `addFeedback` is kept, and its logic moved verbatim into `ownershipFilterOf`.
  - No revert is re-applied.
- `scripts/cost-replay.mjs`: I ran it on `origin/main` and on the branch. Both exit 1 with **byte-identical** output, which is the pre-existing LIN-4177 baseline drift. This change adds no replay drift.

### Tests: re-run and mutation checks (by me, against local mongod 8.2.4)
All `tests/unit/lin-4198-*.test.js`: 111 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. I reverted every mutation and the tree is clean.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `priceRequest` → snapshot path (pricing by harness) | 4 fail (Haiku tier test among them) ✔ |
| drop native `costUsd` precedence | 3 fail ✔ |
| drop the snapshot `crossesThreshold && isRunningTotal` null guard | 4 fail ✔ |
| usage fields `$setOnInsert` instead of `$max` (insert-if-absent) | real mongod: 2 fail; store unit: 4 fail ✔ |
| store zero-token records | 4 fail ✔ |
| drop the 2M bound | 4 fail ✔ |
| drop the ownership filter in `readTakenForUsage` | 2 fail ✔ |
| `rootItemId` from `body.rootItemId` | 3 fail ✔ |
| `rootItemId = itemId` (no `anchorOf`) | 1 fail ✔ |
| projection drops token fields / widens to `itemId`/`updatedAt` | 2 fail each ✔ |
| dispatch usage route accepts the Harbour OS token (`authenticateFeedbackToken`) | 1 fail ✔ |
| remove the E11000 retry | **real mongod: 0 fail**; unit fake: 2 fail |

The retry result is not a defect in the deliverable. I instrumented the retry branch: it was hit 0 times in 5 runs of the concurrent witness on real mongod. MongoDB ≥4.2 retries duplicate-key upserts itself when the filter is an equality on the unique key. The claim the ticket needs, that two concurrent batches leave one document each, therefore holds on real mongod and is witnessed. The retry is defensive (MangoDB, other servers) and only the unit fake pins it. However, the mongod test's header says the concurrent batches "lose inserts to the unique index", which this server does not do. Close-out fix 2 below corrects the wording.

### Deliberate deviations: judged
1. **Usage route refuses the Harbour OS feedback token.** Accepted. `authenticateFeedbackToken` calls `harbourFeedbackTokenStore.validateAndConsume`, so reusing it would spend the token on the first batch and 401 every later one. Ownership is still the feedback rule, and the refusal is pinned (mutation above). The ticket's intent, the same ownership and no new credential kind, is met.
2. **`updatedAt` advances on every repost.** Accepted. It is bookkeeping, figures never move, and `listForAnchors` doesn't project it.
3. **Prefix-redundant `{urlKey, rootItemId}` index.** Accepted: the ticket and the lockstep rule ask for it, and it is cheap on a new collection.
4. **Limiter reuse.** Accepted for piece 1. At most 100 records per call keeps the load bounded.
5. **Commit trailer names Sonnet 5.5 while the workers ran Haiku 5.5.** Cosmetic. Close-out may correct it in the squash message.

### Class check
This change is isolated. It is a new store and route pair. The sibling it could have duplicated, the feedback ownership rule, was extracted and shared rather than forked. The parallel route (runner twin) goes through the same handler, and both routes are tested at HTTP level against an in-memory DB.

### Fixes for close-out (both non-behavioural)
1. `lib/model-pricing.js` ~L340–375: `priceRequest`'s JSDoc block sits directly above `promptTokensOf`'s JSDoc. The two blocks are stacked, `export function priceRequest` has no doc above it, and tooling attaches the wrong text. Move the block starting "Price ONE model request (a stored per-request usage record…" down to sit directly above `export function priceRequest(record)`.
2. `tests/unit/lin-4198-request-usage-mongod.test.js` header (L4–8): replace "two concurrent batches with the same ids (which lose inserts to the unique index and must come out as one document each…)" with wording that says the witness proves the outcome (one document each, largest values). Add that mongod ≥4.2 retries same-key upserts server-side, so the store's E11000 retry is pinned by the unit test (`lin-4198-request-usage-store.test.js`), not by this file.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside (D-registers / indexes, `lib/db-indexes.js`).** Both `request-usage` indexes are built on the production database at boot. CI builds them only in test DBs. **After the deploy:** run `db.getCollection('request-usage').getIndexes()` on prod. It must list `{urlKey:1, rootItemId:1, requestId:1}` with `unique:true` and `{urlKey:1, rootItemId:1}`. If the unique one is missing, concurrent posts could duplicate documents.
- **Inside (D3 intake, both routes live).** Both endpoints are reachable through the deployed auth stack. In production that is the consumer dispatch token, and for the runner twin the proxy token with the `take` grant through the real `routes/proxy.js` mount. CI drives them only through the test app. **After the deploy:** take an item with a runner proxy token and `POST /api/proxy/runner/usage/:id` with `{"records":[{"requestId":"probe-1","model":"claude-haiku-4-5","inputTokens":1}]}`. Expect `200 {applied:["probe-1"],rejected:[]}`, and expect one `request-usage` doc with `rootItemId` equal to the row's anchor. Then post the same body from a different token: expect 404. Delete the probe doc afterwards. Rollback, if the route misbehaves before any producer exists: revert commit `7834e234`. The collection is new and nothing reads it, so the revert is clean until piece 2 (LIN-4199) starts posting.
- **Outside: a producer contract for LIN-4199/LIN-4202, not a defect here.** The intake accepts posts only while the row is `status:'taken'` and taken by the posting token. The runner must post usage within that window, including the final batch around a terminal `[done]` marker, and treat a 404 as "not yours / no longer taken". LIN-4199 already owns the runner side, so close-out should add a note there instead of filing a new ticket.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

Every D1–D5 requirement and witness is present, and every load-bearing path goes red when removed. CI is green on `7834e234`, there is no replay drift, and nothing outside the route and store reads the collection. Close-out should make the two doc/comment fixes above and run the two post-deploy checks.

## Close-out — LIN-4198

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2265, squash commit `9cc5ff9cb8ad05478e1e416e3894df16eba9ecca`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 34a617a9…`. Deployed: harbour.cat footer shows `9cc5ff9c…`. The squash message carries the Sonnet 5.5 trailer (review's cosmetic note 5).

**Final CI:** green on the exact merged head `34a617a946ac7ded469aec9f9791a58d9b35288b` (run 41770355748): Unit tests, E2E 1/4–4/4, Secret scan, CI success all pass. Main push run 41771095478 queued at merge.

**Changes I made after approval (both non-behavioural, commit `34a617a9`)**
1. Review fix 1: `lib/model-pricing.js` — moved `priceRequest`'s JSDoc to sit directly above `export function priceRequest` (it had been stacked over `promptTokensOf`'s). Comment move only.
2. Review fix 2: `tests/unit/lin-4198-request-usage-mongod.test.js` header — now says the concurrent witness proves the outcome (one document each, largest values) and that mongod ≥4.2 retries same-key upserts server-side, so the E11000 retry is pinned by `lin-4198-request-usage-store.test.js`. Comment only.
Re-ran `lin-4198-*` and `model-pricing*` tests locally (203 pass, 0 fail) before pushing; full CI re-run on the new head.

**Ledger**
- *Inside — prod indexes (`request-usage` unique `{urlKey,rootItemId,requestId}` and `{urlKey,rootItemId}`):* **NOT RUN.** Needs `db.getCollection('request-usage').getIndexes()` on the production database; I have no prod mongo access. Operator: run that and confirm both are listed, the first with `unique:true`. If the unique one is missing, concurrent posts could duplicate documents. CI proved the index specs in test DBs.
- *Inside — both routes live through the deployed auth stack:* **partly checked, probe NOT RUN.** After deploy, `POST https://harbour.cat/api/dispatch/usage/x` unauthenticated → `401` (route mounted, auth enforced), and the proxy twin `POST /api/proxy/runner/usage/:id` through my token → `403 TAKE_GRANT_REQUIRED` (route mounted, grant enforced). The full probe review specified (take an item with a take-grant runner token, post `probe-1`, expect `200 {applied:["probe-1"],rejected:[]}` and a doc whose `rootItemId` is the row's anchor; then a different token → 404; delete the probe doc) needs a take-grant token and prod DB access I don't have, and I did not want to write to prod data outside that. Operator: run it. **Named rollback** (review): revert commit `7834e234` (now squash `9cc5ff9c`); the collection is new and nothing reads it, so the revert is clean until LIN-4199 starts posting.
- *Outside — producer contract (post only while `taken` by the posting token; final batch around `[done]`; treat 404 as not-yours):* not filed as a new ticket, per review. Posted as a note on LIN-4199 (comment `6d714641`), which owns the runner side.
- *Unproven by live execution:* the E11000 retry never fires on real mongod 8.2 (0 hits in 5 runs); it is defensive, pinned only by the unit fake. Noted, not a defect.
- Pre-existing: `scripts/cost-replay.mjs` exits 1 byte-identically on main and the branch (LIN-4177 baseline drift); this change adds no drift and fixtures/goldens are unchanged.

**Related tickets:** LIN-4199 got the producer-contract note; it and LIN-4202 remain Todo (still blocked-by this piece's follow-on work, nothing to close). No outside follow-up tickets were filed, so no priority/label calls were needed.

**Description:** pre-prune snapshot confirmed via `/issues/LIN-4198/snapshots` (captured the full original description). The description held no embedded plan/research sections (the plan lives on LIN-4195), so nothing was removed; I appended a short implemented-as-approved stub with the PR link.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** The logic was small: a store, a pricing flag and a validator. The work bound in three places.
- **Registers.** Two new routes meant edits to five route census or sweep files (pinned counts and rows), the erasure universe count, the proxy inventory, and the 503 fault-row guard. Each surfaced as its own failure.
- **Auth.** "Same token auth as feedback" couldn't be done literally. Feedback's middleware spends a single-use Harbour OS token on its first success, and usage arrives in batches.
- **Ownership.** The rule lived inside `addFeedback`'s atomic update, so I had to extract `ownershipFilterOf` before a read could share it. `rootItemId` also needed that row read. And a raw database error from a new read is a 500 until it is wrapped as `DispatchStoreFault`.

My own text-matching census forced some odd naming (`requestUsageStoreFor`, a re-exported constant). Its first file walker scanned nothing.

**2. What I'd have done first:** read the route census tests, the LIN-3805 fault guard and `authenticateFeedbackToken`, before designing the routes. All three changed the design, and I found each one through a failure.

**3. What I'd tidy:**
- Replace the census regex with an import-graph check. Matching text catches comments and import paths.
- Collapse the five pinned route counts into one route manifest the sweeps derive from.
- Give usage its own rate limit rather than borrowing feedback's.
- Drop or justify the prefix-redundant `{urlKey, rootItemId}` index.

**4. The ticket, if the area were how I'd want it.** Routes would declare which credentials they accept, so "consumer token only" would be one line, not a choice of middleware. Registration would be one entry that every census reads. Pricing would be per-record, with the snapshot path as a thin wrapper. The ticket would then be "add a store, a pricing function and one route entry", about a third of the work.

**5. What the ticket or plan got wrong:**
- "Same token auth as feedback" conflicts with batched posts, as above.
- The `{urlKey, rootItemId}` index is redundant with the unique key's prefix. Without it, the unique key answers the same query as a covered scan.
- The E11000 retry is defensive only. A real mongod never raised one across 120 concurrent batches, because the server retries equality upserts itself.
- "Nothing outside the route and store reads it" needed more care in practice: the registers (indexes, erasure) and the tests also name the collection.
- `cost-replay.mjs` can't be a pass/fail witness, because it already exits 1 on HEAD.
- The beat-5 brief set a commit trailer naming a different model from the one running the session.

## Survey 1a q6 (the place)

**Got simpler.**
- `promptTokensOf` is now the one definition of prompt size.
- `ownershipFilterOf` puts the taken-row rule in one place, shared by `addFeedback` and the new read.
- `computeUsageCostUsd` and `priceRequest` share one body.

**Now in two places.**
- The E11000 `bulkWriteWithRetry`, copied rather than shared. It is in `lib/kpi-daily-rollup.js` and `lib/request-usage-store.js`.
- The native-`costUsd` precedence. `lib/session-telemetry.js` checks `typeof === 'number'`; `priceRequest` checks `Number.isFinite`.
- The dispatch route count, pinned in three sweep files, each bumped by hand.

**New, with an awkward home.** `requestUsageStoreFor` lives in the intake module only so that `server.js` dodges the text-matching census. That census will collect allow-list entries as pieces 2 and 4 land.

**Should have learned about it and didn't.** `docs/dispatch-integration.md`, `docs/proxy-integration.md` and `docs/runner-prompt.md` don't mention the usage routes; only the proxy catalogue and the architecture doc do. The rate limiters weren't told usage is a different traffic shape.

**On balance:** about the same, slightly better. The new behaviour is isolated, named and pinned by tests, and two rules that were inline now have one home each. Against that, it added a copied helper, a census that matches text, and more hand-pinned counts. Each makes the next route a little costlier to add.
